audits.title: Evaluation of a minimal sedation protocol using ICU sedative consumption as a monitoring tool: a quality improvement multicenter project.
audits.setting: Ten ICUs in a network of nonteaching hospitals
audits.intervention: Multifaceted minimal sedation programme with multidisciplinary daily rounds and monthly audits of sedative consumption with feedback and benchmarking.

cycle2.result: Length of mechanical ventilation 3.15 ± 4.6 days; mean difference -0.76 (95% CI -1.10 to -0.43).

audits.citation: Ranzani OT, Simpson ES, Augusto TB, Cappi SB, Noritomi DT, AMIL Critical Care Group. Evaluation of a minimal sedation protocol using ICU sedative consumption as a monitoring tool: a quality improvement multicenter project. Crit Care. 2014;18(5):580. doi:10.1186/s13054-014-0580-3. PMID: 25673553.

audits.title: The impact of a quality improvement project to standardize pain, agitation, and withdrawal assessments on the use of morphine and midazolam in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit.
audits.standard: Sedation scores documented every 12 h (post phase started when >60% of patients)
audits.setting: 18-bed medical-surgical-cardiac tertiary paediatric ICU, McGill University Health Centre

cycle1.result: Cumulative midazolam equivalent 3.71 mg/kg/ventilation day; morphine equivalent 3.51 mg/kg/ventilation day.

audits.intervention: PDSA cycles: standardised pain and sedation assessments, standardised sedation goal setting, non-pharmacological strategies, with audit and feedback.

cycle2.result: Midazolam equivalent 2.65 mg/kg/ventilation day (P = 0.009); morphine equivalent 2.57 (P = 0.066).

audits.other_findings: No change in withdrawal syndrome, severe pain or medication cost.
audits.citation: Kongkiattikul L, Dagenais M, Ruo N, Fontela P, Di Genova T, Zavalkoff S. The impact of a quality improvement project to standardize pain, agitation, and withdrawal assessments on the use of morphine and midazolam in the Pediatric Intensive Care Unit. Paediatr Anaesth. 2019;29(4):322-330. doi:10.1111/pan.13591. PMID: 30664310.

audits.title: An audit of propofol administration in the intensive care unit: Infusion pump-recorded versus electronically documented amounts.
audits.standard: Recommended maximum safe propofol dose 4 mg/kg/h; accurate EMR documentation
audits.setting: 14-bed metropolitan intensive care unit, Western Health, Melbourne

cycle1.result: Documented bolus propofol was a median 330 mg less than pump amount; 19 (38%) had no EMR-documented boluses despite receiving one; 2/50 (4%) exceeded 4 mg/kg/h.

audits.other_findings: Total infusion amounts correlated closely between pump and EMR (r = 0.99).
audits.citation: McGain F, Lam K, Bates S, Towns M, French C. An audit of propofol administration in the intensive care unit: Infusion pump-recorded versus electronically documented amounts. Aust Crit Care. 2020;33(1):25-29. doi:10.1016/j.aucc.2018.12.005. PMID: 30770268.

audits.title: A Quality Improvement Project to Increase Adherence to a Pain, Agitation, and Delirium Protocol in the Intensive Care Unit.
audits.standard: Existing pain, agitation and delirium (PAD) protocol and clinical practice guidelines
audits.setting: ICU, Duke Regional Hospital; chart audit
audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary educational module: online tutorial, point-of-care reminders, written materials and verbal coaching.

cycle2.result: PAD protocol use decreased to 41%, although compliance with PAD clinical practice guidelines reportedly increased.

audits.other_findings: Protocol use unexpectedly decreased; authors suggest reviewing the protocol.
audits.citation: Yan W, Morgan BT, Berry P, Matthys MK, Thompson JA, Smallheer BA. A Quality Improvement Project to Increase Adherence to a Pain, Agitation, and Delirium Protocol in the Intensive Care Unit. Dimens Crit Care Nurs. 2019;38(3):174-181. doi:10.1097/dcc.0000000000000353. PMID: 30946126.

audits.title: Quality improvement project aimed at improving the reliability of spontaneous awakening trials in a district general intensive care unit.
audits.standard: Critical care guidelines recommending light sedation with a daily sedation hold (spontaneous awakening trial); project target 80% of eligible patients
audits.setting: 10-bed combined ICU/HDU, Hairmyres Hospital, NHS Lanarkshire, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Median 47% of SAT-eligible patients received a sedation hold; mean RASS -2.3; 7 ventilated days and 10 unit days on average

audits.intervention: Multidisciplinary sedation hold protocol based on the 'Wake up and breathe' guidelines, tested in PDSA cycles, with staff education, consultant prompting and a daily audit form

cycle2.result: 96% of SAT-eligible patients received a sedation break; ventilation 5.5 days and unit stay 8 days; no adverse events

audits.other_findings: During PDSA testing 65% then 79% received holds. Average RASS did not improve (-2.4), and medical staff were less aware of the protocol than nurses.
audits.citation: Ferraioli D, Ferguson L, Carberry M. Quality improvement project aimed at improving the reliability of spontaneous awakening trials in a district general intensive care unit. BMJ Open Qual. 2019;8(2):e000518. doi:10.1136/bmjoq-2018-000518. PMID: 31206059.
